children: Index Saudi Arabia, the country's leading trade show for interiors, furniture, and fit-out, opens today (September 15) in Riyadh under the theme “Built on heritage. Designed for tomorrow,” bringing together some of the top global architects, interior designers, real estate developers and international design experts for the 2026 edition.

The three-day event is being held at Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center (RICEC), with the Architecture and Design Commission as Strategic Partner. This year's edition will place Saudi design leadership, cultural identity and emerging talent at the centre of its programme.

Reflecting this year's theme, sessions will explore how Saudi heritage and cultural identity are being translated into contemporary projects, alongside practical and commercial priorities including materiality, technology, evolving client expectations and project delivery.

Its key event - Index Design Talks - will bring together more than 60 leading architects, interior designers, real estate developers and international design experts to examine the ideas and priorities shaping the kingdom’s design and fit-out sector.
Saudi speakers will represent more than half of the programme, bringing local perspectives to discussions around the Kingdom's evolving design identity, said the organisers, dmg events.

Index Future Stars, to be held in collaboration with ArchiNet, will bring a next-generation perspective to the programme, with final-year interior design students from 11 Saudi universities presenting their projects to a panel of established design professionals.
Competing for the opportunity to secure an internship, the initiative creates a direct link between design education, emerging Saudi talent and professional practice.

The judging panel includes senior figures from Athel Design, ROSHN, Naslaa, Ithra, Adeera Hospitality, Buro Happold and Realm Design, bringing expertise from across architecture, design, development and the built environment.

Returning for a second year, Trend Tours will take visitors directly to standout products, materials and design solutions across the exhibition through expert-led tours developed with CIOB, RIBA and Index Brand Ambassadors, stated the organisers.

Combining curated stand visits, product demonstrations and direct interaction with brands and designers, the tours will help visitors explore key trends and applications across the show floor, it stated.
Elaine O’Connell, Senior Vice President – Design and Hospitality Division at dmg events, said: "Saudi Arabia’s design story is increasingly being shaped by its own identity and talent."

"At Index Saudi Arabia, we want to create space for both – bringing established industry leaders together with the next generation of Saudi designers, while exploring how the Kingdom's heritage can inform the spaces being created for its future," she stated.

Beyond its features programme, Index Saudi Arabia will provide a major sourcing and business platform for the kingdom’s interiors and fit-out market, connecting architects, interior designers, buyers, hotel operators, procurement teams and project owners with global and regional suppliers across furniture, interiors, materials and fit-out solutions, she added.

title: ZAWYA: Saudi design leaders, emerging talent set the agenda at Index expo
